title: Labeling oddities field notebook
body:
Quick log of odd labeling decisions, heuristics I keep returning to. Personal notebook — messy; use for ad-hoc decisions and to capture examples for next guidelines draft.

Context / goal:
- We need practical rules that reduce annotator variance for conversational and mixed-content items (code snippets + emojis + PII-like tokens). Not trying to be exhaustive, just useful stopgaps.

Common micro-decisions (my current take):
1) Trailing punctuation on spans: include punctuation only when it changes meaning (e.g., "U.S." keep dots inside abbreviation span; for names followed by comma or period, exclude trailing " , . " unless annotating full string literal).

2) Emojis as labels: treat emoji as their own token. If emoji conveys additional intent separate from surrounding text, label it as SEPARATE. Example: "Nice job 👍" -> label sentiment span for "Nice job" and label emoji as nonverbal-token.

3) Code + comments: when snippet appears inline (backticks or monospace), annotate the human language part only. If the label taxonomy includes code-intent (e.g., BUG vs EXAMPLE), add meta-tag but do not split tokens inside identifiers.

4) Dates & partial dates: prefer normalized date spans only when unambiguous. "May 2023" -> DATE; "05/03" -> mark as AMBIGUOUS_DATE unless ISO context present.

5) Phone numbers & IDs: annotate sequences of digits as PII only if length & structure match known patterns AND additional context suggests personal identifier. Avoid labeling account-like strings that are product codes (e.g., SKU-1234) unless preceded by words like "account" or "phone".

6) Nested mention heuristics: allow ONE level of nesting (person -> role), but flatten deeper nesting by labeling outermost meaningful chunk. If annotators disagree, prefer longer span (conservative recall).

Sampling heuristics for audit:
- Pull 300 items by stratified buckets: short (<20 chars), medium, long (>200 chars); include 15% with code blocks; 10% with emojis; 20% with numeric-heavy tokens. Flagging threshold: if disagreement > 20% in any bucket -> create mini-annotation workshop for that wedge.

Quick examples collected today (decision notes inline):
- "Call me at 555-1234." -> label "555-1234" AS PII_PHONE (context: "Call me" indicates personal phone).
- "Order #559-XY is delayed" -> DO NOT label as PII, mark as ORDER_CODE.
- "Can u send pass: hunter2" -> label "hunter2" as potential credential (sensitive); if no real-world pattern, tag SUSPICIOUS_CRED.
- "I live in San Jose, CA." -> label "San Jose" as LOCATION; include state if present.

Open questions / followups to fold into guideline draft:
- How to annotate anonymized placeholders generated by upstream masking? (e.g., "[NAME_REDACTED]") My impulse: label as REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER with original type if available in metadata.
- Explicit rule for mixed-language spans (en/es): should we split spans per language or use language-agnostic labels? Leaning language-agnostic for entity types, but capture language in metadata for evaluation.
- Edge case: concatenated tokens without separators ("JohnSmith2023"). When length > 8 and pattern looks like name+year, split heuristically; else annotate whole as OTHER_IDENTIFIER. Need small regex test and list of false positives.

Tiny regex cheats I keep using (for my own sampling scripts):
- phone-ish: "\b\d{3}[- ]?\d{3}[- ]?\d{4}\b"
- order id: "\b[A-Z]{2,}-?\d{2,}\b"
- redacted placeholder: "\[[A-Z_]+\]"

To do (short):
- Run quick 1k sample with these regexes and compute annotator agreement per bucket.
- Draft 1-page decision table from above micro-decisions and circulate with labeling team.
- Add 20 golden examples to test suite (mix of emojis, inline code, PII-like tokens).

Notes to self: keep this file short and messy. When I formalize, move canonical examples to confluence and link here. Also remind SEs to not rely on exact string-matching heuristics in production models; these are annotation-time heuristics only.

End of notes.
